newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs recover as rate fears dampened.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs recover as rate fears dampened.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures firmed on Thursday on buying back after the previous day's sharp sell-off.
Dealers said comments by Japanese Finance Ministry and Bank of Japan (BOJ) officials endorsing the central bank's current easy monetary policy helped the recovery.

Japanese markets came under intense pressure on Wednesday after BOJ deputy governor Toshihiko Fukui was quoted as saying the central bank was considering the right timing to raise the official discount rate.
A senior BOJ official later said Fukui had been misquoted and that there were no immediate plans to raise rates.

Dealers said the Euroyen market saw active spread trades, with players selling the forward months like March'98 and June'98 on the perception that Japanese rates would be on their way up by next year.
"They think that once the BOJ hikes, there'll be speculation of more hikes," a trader with a European futures house said.
He said the lead December Euroyen contract would face resistance around 98.97/98. It was quoted at 98.91 at 1120 GMT against its IMM close at 98.90 on volume of 8,893 lots.
March was at 98.70 against 98.68 on 13,340 lots.
June JGBs settled at 123.95 against their previous 123.82. Resistance was seen at 124.35.

News that Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd had incurred losses of 10 billion yen in derivatives trading at its London branch gave a lift to JGBs but the impact was limited as the loss was seen as insignificant for a bank that size, dealers said.
Eurodollar futures dipped in thin trade but dealers said the market looked well supported after the Federal Reserve decision to leave short-term rates unchanged at its meeting on Tuesday.
September Eurodollars finished at 93.960 against their IMM close at 93.960 on volume of 7,270 lots.
